description: This vibrant Ceviche de Camaron is a refreshing Mexican classic, featuring succulent shrimp marinated in fresh lime juice until perfectly "cooked". Mixed with crisp vegetables like cucumber, tomato, onion, and cilantro, it offers a burst of zesty, savory flavors. A perfect dish for warm weather or as a light, flavorful appetizer.

ingredients.item: Shrimp, raw, peeled, deveined, tail off

instructions.title: Prepare the Shrimp
instructions.text: Rinse shrimp under cold water and pat dry. Cut each shrimp into small, bite-sized pieces (about 1/2 inch). Place the chopped shrimp in a non-reactive bowl.

instructions.title: Marinate the Shrimp
instructions.text: Pour the fresh lime juice over the shrimp, ensuring all pieces are submerged. Stir gently. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or until the shrimp turn opaque and pink, resembling cooked shrimp. This can take up to 1-2 hours depending on shrimp size.

instructions.title: Prepare the Vegetables
instructions.text: While the shrimp marinates, finely dice the red onion, tomatoes, and cucumber. Chop the fresh cilantro. If using, finely mince the jalapeno or serrano pepper.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Once the shrimp is "cooked" by the lime juice, drain about half of the excess lime juice from the bowl. Add the diced red onion, tomatoes, cucumber, cilantro, and minced pepper (if using) to the shrimp.

instructions.title: Season and Mix
instructions.text: Season the ceviche generously with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir all ingredients together gently to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed, adding more lime juice if desired for extra tang.

instructions.title: Chill and Serve
instructions.text: Cover the ceviche and refrigerate for another 15-20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Just before serving, gently fold in the diced avocado. Serve immediately with tostadas or tortilla chips.

tips: For the best flavor, always use fresh squeezed lime juice. Bottled lime juice will not yield the same vibrant taste or proper acidity for "cooking" the shrimp.
If you prefer a milder flavor, remove the seeds and veins from the jalapeno or serrano pepper, or omit it entirely. For extra zest, add a pinch of dried oregano.
Ceviche is best enjoyed fresh on the day it is made. Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one day. Do not freeze.
article:
Ceviche de Camaron, often simply called Shrimp Ceviche, is a vibrant and refreshing Mexican seafood dish that captures the essence of coastal cuisine. Imagine plump, succulent shrimp, "cooked" to perfection in the tangy embrace of fresh lime juice, then tossed with a colorful medley of crisp vegetables and aromatic herbs. It’s a dish that tantalizes the taste buds, offering a burst of freshness with every bite, making it a beloved staple from bustling beachside stands to elegant dining tables across Mexico and beyond.

Perfect for warm weather, entertaining, or simply a healthy and flavorful meal, this easy-to-make dish brings the spirit of Mexico right into your kitchen. Far from complicated, the beauty of Shrimp Ceviche lies in its simplicity and the quality of its fresh ingredients.

## What is Shrimp Ceviche?

At its heart, Shrimp Ceviche is a culinary masterpiece of fresh ingredients, where raw seafood is marinated in citrus juices, most commonly lime. This acidic marinade chemically "cooks" the protein, turning it opaque and firm, similar to what heat would do, but without any actual cooking over a flame. While ceviche traditions vary across Latin America, Mexican Shrimp Ceviche typically distinguishes itself with a generous use of tomatoes, onions, cilantro, and often a touch of spicy jalapeño or serrano pepper, creating a robust and deeply flavorful profile. It's a dish that celebrates the ocean's bounty, offering a light yet satisfying experience that's both nutritious and incredibly delicious.

## Ingredients for Ceviche de Camaron

The foundation of a great Shrimp Ceviche lies in its fresh, high-quality components. Here’s what you’ll need to create this Mexican culinary delight:

*   **Shrimp:** 1 ½ pounds, raw, fresh, peeled, and deveined. Medium to large shrimp work best.
*   **Limes:** 10-12 medium-sized limes, freshly squeezed. This is non-negotiable for authentic flavor.
*   **Red Onion:** 1 small, finely diced. Red onion adds a beautiful color and a mild, sweet bite.
*   **Roma Tomatoes:** 2-3 medium, seeded and finely diced. Roma tomatoes are firm and less watery, ideal for ceviche.
*   **Cilantro:** ½ cup, fresh, chopped. The quintessential herb for Mexican cuisine, adding a bright, herbaceous note.
*   **Jalapeño or Serrano Pepper:** 1-2, finely diced (seeds removed for less heat, or left in for more). Adjust to your spice preference.
*   **Cucumber:** 1 small, peeled, seeded, and finely diced (optional, but adds a refreshing crunch).
*   **Salt:** To taste.
*   **Black Pepper:** To taste.
*   **Optional Add-ins:** Diced avocado for creaminess, a dash of Clamato (tomato-clam juice) for an extra layer of savory flavor, or a pinch of dried oregano.

## How to Make Mexican Shrimp Ceviche: Step-by-Step

Mastering how to make Mexican Shrimp Ceviche is simpler than you might think. Follow these steps for a perfect batch:

1.  **Prepare the Shrimp:** Start by thoroughly cleaning your shrimp. Peel and devein them, then rinse under cold water. Pat them dry with paper towels. Cut the shrimp into small, bite-sized pieces (about ½ inch chunks). This ensures they "cook" evenly and quickly in the lime juice.
2.  **Marinate the Shrimp:** Place the chopped shrimp in a non-reactive bowl (glass, ceramic, or stainless steel works best). Pour enough freshly squeezed lime juice over the shrimp to completely submerge them. Stir gently to ensure all pieces are coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 1 hour. The shrimp will turn opaque pink as the acid "cooks" it. For very small pieces, 30 minutes is usually sufficient; larger pieces might need up to an hour. Avoid over-marinating, which can make the shrimp rubbery.
3.  **Prepare the Vegetables:** While the shrimp is marinating, finely dice the red onion, tomatoes, cucumber (if using), and jalapeño/serrano pepper. Roughly chop the fresh cilantro.
4.  **Combine Ingredients:** Once the shrimp is opaque, you can drain some of the lime juice if you prefer a less "soupy" ceviche, leaving just enough to keep it moist. Add the diced onion, tomatoes, cilantro, cucumber, and jalapeño to the bowl with the shrimp.
5.  **Season and Mix:** Season generously with salt and black pepper. Stir all the ingredients together gently until well combined. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. If using, now is the time to add avocado or Clamato.
6.  **Chill and Serve:** For optimal flavor, cover the bowl again and refrigerate the ceviche for at least another 15-30 minutes. This allows the flavors to meld beautifully and ensures it’s perfectly chilled for serving.

## Expert Tips for Perfect Ceviche

Crafting the perfect Shrimp Ceviche requires attention to a few key details that elevate it from good to unforgettable:

*   **Freshness is Paramount:** The quality of your shrimp makes all the difference. Always opt for the freshest, highest-quality shrimp you can find. If using frozen shrimp, thaw it completely in the refrigerator and pat it very dry before dicing.
*   **Only Fresh Lime Juice:** Bottled lime juice simply doesn’t compare. Freshly squeezed lime juice is essential for both flavor and the chemical "cooking" process.
*   **Don't Over-Marinate:** While the lime juice "cooks" the shrimp, too much time in the acid can make the shrimp tough and rubbery. Keep an eye on the shrimp and remove it once it turns opaque.
*   **Uniform Dicing:** Chopping all your vegetables and shrimp to a similar size ensures every bite is balanced and the flavors are evenly distributed.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your ceviche before serving. Adjust the salt, pepper, and spice level as needed. A squeeze of extra lime juice right before serving can also brighten the flavors.
*   **Keep it Chilled:** Ceviche is best served very cold. Make sure to chill it thoroughly before serving, and keep it on ice if serving outdoors on a warm day.
*   **Use a Non-Reactive Bowl:** Acidic ingredients like lime juice can react with certain metals, imparting a metallic taste. Glass, ceramic, or stainless steel bowls are ideal for marinating.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Enjoying your homemade Shrimp Ceviche is all about the presentation and accompaniments. Traditionally, it’s served with crispy corn tostadas or saltine crackers, providing a delightful textural contrast to the tender shrimp and crunchy vegetables.

*   **Classic Accompaniments:** Offer extra lime wedges, your favorite Mexican hot sauce (like Valentina or Tapatío), and perhaps a side of sliced avocado for a creamy counterpoint.
*   **Creative Uses:** Beyond tostadas, Shrimp Ceviche makes a fantastic topping for tacos, a refreshing side salad, or even served in crisp lettuce cups for a low-carb option.
*   **Drink Pairings:** A cold Mexican lager beer, a zesty Michelada, or a crisp, dry white wine like Sauvignon Blanc or Albariño would perfectly complement the vibrant flavors of the ceviche. For non-alcoholic options, sparkling water with a slice of lime is wonderfully refreshing.

## Variations and Substitutions

While this recipe focuses on the classic Mexican Shrimp Ceviche, the world of ceviche offers endless possibilities for customization:

*   **Different Seafood:** You can easily substitute or combine shrimp with other firm white fish (like snapper, cod, or mahi-mahi), scallops, or even octopus. Just ensure all seafood is very fresh.
*   **Spice Level:** For more heat, leave some seeds in your jalapeño, or add a finely minced serrano or even a touch of habanero pepper. A pinch of red pepper flakes can also work.
*   **Flavor Boosters:** Some recipes include a dash of Worcestershire sauce or a splash of orange juice for a slightly different tang.
*   **Fruity Twists:** For a sweet and tangy contrast, consider adding finely diced mango or pineapple to your ceviche. This is particularly popular in some coastal regions.
*   **Regional Influences:** While Mexican ceviche is often tomato-heavy, other Latin American versions vary greatly. Peruvian ceviche, for example, often includes sweet potato and corn, while Ecuadorian versions might feature more tomato sauce and popcorn.
*   **Vegetarian Option:** For a plant-based alternative, try using diced hearts of palm, firm mushrooms, or even cooked chickpeas "marinated" in the lime and vegetable mixture.

Whether you're hosting a party, craving a taste of the ocean, or simply looking for a healthy and flavorful meal, Shrimp Ceviche delivers a refreshing culinary experience. Its vibrant colors, zesty flavors, and satisfying textures make it an irresistible dish that’s surprisingly easy to master. So grab your freshest ingredients, squeeze those limes, and prepare to be transported to the sunny coasts of Mexico with every delicious bite!
